downstream_reviews.snippet: [F2] Each $L_t$ maps $X$ boundedly into $Y$, with a bound uniform in $t$: $\|L_tu\|_{C^{0,\alpha}}\le C_L\|u\|_{C^{2,\alpha}}$ for $u\in X$ and $t\in[0,1]$, because the coefficients are bounded in $C^{0,\alpha}$ and the principal matrices $A_t=tA+(1-t)I$ are uniformly elliptic with constants $\min\{\lambda,1\},\max\{\Lambda,1\}$, $C^{0,\alpha}$ seminorm at most $K$ and lower-order coefficient bounds at most $M$. downstream_reviews.snippet: [F4] Linear normalization and ellipsoid-to-ball geometry. If $A_0$ is symmetric positive definite with spectrum in $[\lambda,\Lambda]$, put $S=A_0^{1/2}$ and $v(y)=w(x+Sy)$. Then $A_0:D_x^2w(x+Sy)=\Delta_yv(y)$, $\|S\|\le\sqrt\Lambda$ and $\|S^{-1}\|\le1/\sqrt\lambda$ ([[def-uniformly-elliptic-nondivergence-operator]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]). For every $r>0$, $S(B_{r/\sqrt\Lambda})\subseteq B_r$ and $B_{\theta_{\rm geo}r}\subseteq S(B_{r/(2\sqrt\Lambda)})$ with $\theta_{\rm geo}:=\frac12\sqrt{\lambda/\Lambda}$. Consequently, for every $0<\theta\le\theta_{\rm geo}$, the Poisson estimate on $B_{r/\sqrt\Lambda}$ controls the original solution on $B_{\theta r}$, with norm-comparison constants depending only on $\lambda,\Lambda$.

downstream_reviews.affected_use: The nondivergence operator Lu in the W^{2,p} estimate and the flattened principal and lower-order coefficients use the matrix and derivative contraction.
downstream_reviews.snippet: [F7] Local $C^{1,1}$ flattening. Here $C^{1,1}$ means that each local boundary graph is $C^1$ and its first derivatives are Lipschitz on compact patches. The flattening map is a shear with determinant one; its first derivative and inverse are bounded, and its second weak derivatives are essentially bounded: apply the real-valued converse of [[thm-w-one-infinity-functions-have-lipschitz-representatives]] to each Lipschitz graph-gradient component on a smaller convex base box. For smooth $w$, mollify the graph on a slightly larger base box. The graph functions and gradients converge uniformly; their uniformly bounded second derivatives converge locally in each finite $L^p$ to the weak second derivatives. Apply the ordinary chain rule to the smooth shears, then pass to the weak derivative identities using change of variables and these convergences. This gives $D(w\circ\Phi)=(Dw\circ\Phi)D\Phi$ and $D^2(w\circ\Phi)=(D^2w\circ\Phi)[D\Phi,D\Phi]+(Dw\circ\Phi)D^2\Phi$. The change-of-variables formula and the bound $\|gh\|_{L^p}\le\|g\|_{L^\infty}\|h\|_{L^p}$ therefore bound the local $W^{1,p}$ and $W^{2,p}$ norms of the pullback by the corresponding original norms, with constants controlled by the chart bounds. For general $w\in W^{2,p}$, smooth approximation on the open chart patch ([[thm-meyers-serrin-density-on-an-arbitrary-open-set]]) and weak stability of derivatives ([[lem-weak-stability-of-sobolev-derivatives]]) give the same weak chain rule and estimate. The Jacobian and chart derivatives are controlled on the finite atlas of the bounded $C^{1,1}$ domain ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]], [[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]], [[thm-holder-inequality-for-integrals]]). The transformed lower-order coefficients are bounded by the original bounds and the chart's $C^{1,1}$ bounds. ([[def-uniformly-elliptic-nondivergence-operator]])

downstream_reviews.snippet: [F2] If $A_0$ is a symmetric positive-definite matrix with spectrum in $[\lambda,\Lambda]$ and $w\in W^{2,p}(\mathbb R^n)$, put $S=A_0^{1/2}$, $\Phi(y)=x_0+Sy$, and $v=w\circ\Phi$. Testing the weak-derivative identities and changing variables by $\Phi$ gives $D_{y_i}v=\sum_k S_{ki}(D_{x_k}w)\circ\Phi$ and $D_{y_i y_j}^2v=\sum_{k,\ell}S_{ki}S_{\ell j}(D_{x_kx_\ell}^2w)\circ\Phi$ as $L^p$ classes; thus $v\in W^{2,p}(\mathbb R^n)$. The change-of-variables formula gives $\|g\circ\Phi\|_{L^p(dy)}=|\det S|^{-1/p}\|g\|_{L^p(dx)}$, so the Hessian norms before and after pullback are equivalent with constants depending only on $n,p,\lambda,\Lambda$, since $\|S\|\le\sqrt\Lambda$ and $\|S^{-1}\|\le\lambda^{-1/2}$. Finally $\Delta_yv=(A_0:D_x^2w)\circ\Phi$. Therefore the global Laplacian estimate [F1] gives $\|D^2w\|_{L^p}\le C(n,p,\lambda,\Lambda)\|A_0:D^2w\|_{L^p}$. ([[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]], [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], [[def-uniformly-elliptic-nondivergence-operator]])

downstream_reviews.affected_use: Subtracting the boundary extension gives Lw=f-Lg, whose Holder bound uses the coefficient matrix contracted with D^2g.
downstream_reviews.snippet:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $n\ge2$, $0<\alpha<1$, let $\Omega$ be a bounded $C^{2,\alpha}$ domain, and let $L=a^{ij}\partial_i\partial_j+b^i\partial_i+c$ be uniformly elliptic on $\bar\Omega$ with constants $\lambda,\Lambda$, $[A]_{0,\alpha;\Omega}\le K$, and $b,c\in C^{0,\alpha}(\bar\Omega)$ with $\|b\|_{C^{0,\alpha}}+\|c\|_{C^{0,\alpha}}\le M$. Let $u\in C^2(\Omega)\cap C^0(\bar\Omega)$, $g\in C^{2,\alpha}(\bar\Omega)$ and $f\in C^{0,\alpha}(\bar\Omega)$ satisfy $Lu=f$ in $\Omega$ and $u=g$ on $\partial\Omega$. Then $u\in C^{2,\alpha}(\bar\Omega)$ and
$$\|u\|_{C^{2,\alpha}(\bar\Omega)}\le C\bigl(\|u\|_{C^0(\Omega)}+\|f\|_{C^{0,\alpha}(\bar\Omega)}+\|g\|_{C^{2,\alpha}(\bar\Omega)}\bigr),$$
where $C=C(n,\alpha,\lambda,\Lambda,K,M,\Omega)$ depends on $\Omega$ only through a finite $C^{2,\alpha}$ chart atlas and its radii. The coefficient assumptions include the H\"older norms needed for the lower-order products, and no solvability is asserted: the estimate is a regularity statement for the given classical solution.
